explanation: Bowing — sometimes paired with a handshake in business settings — is the standard Japanese greeting, and cheek kissing isn't part of everyday social custom. It mainly appears in formal diplomatic contexts, like meetings between heads of state, so using it in an ordinary social setting can come across as oddly intimate or foreign.
local_tip: Default to a bow, or a soft handshake if one is offered first, and don't initiate a cheek kiss unless your host clearly does.

also_check.note: La bise (cheek kissing) is a standard greeting among friends and acquaintances, varying by region in number of kisses.
Cheek kissing is not a traditional greeting and can feel overly familiar; bowing or a handshake is preferred.
A single cheek kiss is a common, friendly greeting, especially among women or in social settings.
